title: [bug] the Notes rename destroyed the stored document, and load overwrote bytes it could not read
design:
Happened for real, 2026-09-05, in this repo, to the user's own notes. Recorded
because the second half is the part worth remembering.

## What happened

ccp-ydo.1 renamed NotesDocument's `pads` property to `notes`. The type is
Codable with synthesised keys, so the stored JSON key changed with it. Every
document already on disk says "pads", so decoding returned nil.

## Why that was fatal rather than annoying

NotesAdapter.loadApplyingRetention did:

    let decoded = data.flatMap { try? JSONDecoder().decode(...) }
    var loaded = decoded?.sanitized(...) ?? .initial(...)
    if loaded == decoded { ... } else { _ = persist(loaded) }

decoded == nil, so `loaded` is a fresh empty document, and `persist` wrote it
straight over the user's bytes ON LOAD — before a keystroke, before the panel
was even looked at. Three tabs of notes gone in the first launch of the renamed
build. No Time Machine destination and no APFS local snapshots on this machine,
so nothing to restore from.

## Fixed

1. NotesDocument now pins CodingKeys: `case notes = "pads"`. The Swift name and
   the wire name are decoupled, permanently, with a comment saying why. It also
   reads back the "notes" key one build wrote.
2. Load no longer persists over data it failed to decode. It shows an empty
   document, leaves the stored bytes untouched, and the first real write moves
   them to `scratchpadDocument.unreadable` rather than over them.
3. Tests/CCPKitTests/NotesDocumentStorageTests.swift covers all four: pads
   decodes, notes decodes, encoding stays pads, and neither load nor the first
   edit destroys unreadable bytes.

## The general lesson, worth more than the fix

A rename is a data migration whenever the renamed thing is Codable, and a
decode failure must never be resolved by writing. Both halves are now trapped in
bd remember. Any type in this repo that is persisted and gets renamed needs the
same CodingKeys treatment — NotesDocument was the only one, checked.
close_reason: CodingKeys pin notes to the on-disk "pads" and also read back the "notes" key the broken build wrote; load no longer persists over bytes it failed to decode, and the first real edit moves them to scratchpadDocument.unreadable rather than over them. Four regression tests in NotesDocumentStorageTests. Both lessons in bd remember. The user's own three tabs were NOT recoverable — no Time Machine destination and no APFS snapshots on this machine.

title: NoteStore: platform-agnostic storage behind a one-line backend swap
description:
The scratchpad stops storing text in UserDefaults entirely. Craft becomes the store, reached through a platform-agnostic protocol so swapping to Obsidian or Notion is a one-line change at the composition root.

Decided by the user: no local truth. UserDefaults keeps only configuration (retention, selection, the pad-to-document mapping) — never the note text.

The protocol is the deliverable, not the Craft call. Shape it around what any note backend can honour — list notes, read one, write one, create, delete, a modified date — and keep every Craft noun (spaces, folders, block ids) inside CraftNoteStore. If the protocol mentions a block, it has leaked.

Async throwing, per CLAUDE.md. A store that is offline or unauthenticated is a normal state the widget renders, not an error that empties the pad — with no local truth, a failed read must never present as an empty note the user then types over.

Supersedes the earlier 'local truth, Craft as mirror' framing.

title: Craft POST merges into adjacent block instead of creating one
description: POSTing a new text block at the head of a non-empty Craft document does not create a block. Both position spellings tried merge the text into the adjacent block instead: start+pageId merges into the top block (observed first), before+siblingId against the sidecar head merges into the beginning of the same block (observed second, consistently). Appends (after+siblingId, end+pageId into empty docs) work and create separate blocks, so this is specific to head insertion. The pad holds the truth throughout; the playground doc shows the merged state. Do not type top-inserts at the pad until this resolves — each attempt compounds the merge.
design: Next hypotheses, cheapest first: (1) send pageId ALONGSIDE siblingId in the before position object — all vendor position examples that work carry a page context except sibling ones; the upload endpoint takes them as separate query params so this is a guess; (2) ask whether Craft joins consecutive same-style text blocks on write and whether a type or separator prevents it; (3) PUT-replace shaping (fold the new slice into the head block deliberately, then split) — last resort, breaks 1:1 slice identity. Recorded product rule for the splitter (ccp-xgl): a regular return starts a new block, shift+return is a soft newline inside the same block, exactly like Craft. That distinction currently does not exist in the pad-to-blocks join and must land with whatever fix comes out of this bead.
close_reason: fixed: head inserts post at end then PUT /blocks/move before the head. Live-proven on the playground doc (single + 3-block batches land separate and in order; 4 probe blocks deleted, doc restored to 12 children). Hypothesis 1 (pageId+siblingId) dead by live 400 invalid_union + api-docs union; before-mid-doc confirmed working so the bug was head-only.

title: Messages widget spike: IMsgCore eval plus reply-thread and tapback send verdict
description: Spike: can CCP host most of Apple Messages via imsg's IMsgCore (MIT, Swift 6)? No public Messages API exists. Reads come from ~/Library/Messages/chat.db (SQLite WAL, read-only, FSEvents+poll watch) behind Full Disk Access; sends ride Messages.app AppleScript behind Automation permission with Messages.app running. Beyond that (edit/unsend, read receipts, typing, group mgmt) is SIP-disabled injection -- excluded. Spike tasks: (1) add IMsgCore as pinned URL dep in a scratch target, list chats, read a thread, search; (2) send a text to self via AppleScript; (3) attempt send-as-reply (reply_to_guid is documented read-only -- expect fallback to plain send, confirm); (4) attempt standard tapback send; (5) parse attributedBody + ns-since-2001 timestamps on a real db; (6) pin-vs-fork call on IMsgCore. Verdicts gate ccp-messages-read / -send scope. UI direction (native widget, NOT a carried screen like psymail): WidgetCard + WidgetHeader, content is HStack of avatar rail + thread view. Rail is a single avatar column; hover >1s expands a floating names+previews panel via .overlay (layout-unaffecting); default selection is the most-recent chat with its avatar highlighted. Permissions degrade to inline grant states (FDA mandatory for history; Automation for send; Contacts optional with handle-initials fallback).
notes: SPIKE VERDICT (2026-09-05, imsg @ main, scratch build in /tmp): IMsgCore CONSUMABLE -- library product, MIT, tagged to v0.9.0 (pin exact, do not fork: schema drift handled in-lib via column detection, upstream active). Transitive lib deps only SQLite.swift + PhoneNumberKit (both MIT, GPL-compatible); Commander is CLI-only. Proven: scratch pkg depending on IMsgCore builds clean under Swift 6.3.3 in ~17s. Read surface (public on MessageStore): listChats, chatInfo, participants, messages(chatID:limit:filter:), messagesAfter cursor pagination, searchMessages, attachments, messageSendStatus, enriched reply context (replyToGUID/Text/Sender) + reaction metadata, TypedStreamParser for attributedBody, MessageWatcher AsyncThrowingStream (FSEvents + 5s poll fallback, includeReactions, per-chat + sinceRowID resume), ContactResolver over CNContactStore with graceful fallback. Send: MessageSender.send(recipient/text/attachmentPath/service/region/chatGUID) via bounded osascript child Process -- TCC attributes to CCP bundle (stable signing keeps grants). VERDICT send-as-reply: NOT POSSIBLE on public surface (no reply param anywhere; AppleScript send has no reply target) -- display threading only, replies land as plain thread messages. VERDICT tapback send: NOT VIABLE (CLI-only ReactCommand drives System Events UI automation: activates Messages.app stealing focus, needs Accessibility, most-recent-message only) -- tapback display fully supported. FDA confirmed mandatory live: read-only open of ~/Library/Messages/chat.db -> authorization denied without FDA. NOT live-tested: actual send + Automation prompt flow (needs Messages sign-in + user-approved prompt; deferred to send bead).
close_reason: Spike complete: IMsgCore consumable (library, MIT, pin exact v0.9.0, scratch build passes). Send-as-reply impossible on public surface (display threading only); tapback send not viable for CCP (System Events UI automation, needs Accessibility + steals focus). FDA confirmed mandatory live. title: the selected tab and the note container share one continuous silhouette
design:
The visual heart of ccp-ydo. The selected tab is elevated above the notes card,
and its right border dissolves into the note container floating alongside — the
two read as one object, two objects only when you look at the unselected tabs.

Do not abut two RoundedRectangles: the join shows a hairline, and each piece
casts its own shadow into the other. Build the union as one Shape (a Path with
the outer corners rounded and the inner join carrying the small concave fillet
that makes it read as continuous — the same trick a browser tab bar uses), fill
it once, and draw elevation once over the whole path.

Selection must ANIMATE between tabs — the shape's join slides to the newly
selected row rather than cutting. Per CLAUDE.md this is one of the places worth
animating: it shows the eye where the note came from.
close_reason: NoteJoinedShape unions the note's rounded rect with the selected tab (left corners rounded, running one radius past the rail so the union has overlap) into a single Path. Fill, stroke and shadow each drawn once over that outline — no hairline, no doubled shadow. tabTop is animatableData, so selecting another note slides the join. Verified in a live capture.

title: [epic] Notes: rename the scratchpad and rebuild its chrome as two overlapping containers
design:
Specified by the user 2026-09-05. The scratchpad becomes NOTES, and its chrome
stops being one flat card with a horizontal tab strip. It becomes two objects
that overlap and read as one continuous shape, the way Apple's Notes reads:

  ┌─ Notes ──────────────────── [↗] ┐   ← the notes card: header + toolbar
  │ ┌────────┐                       │
  │ │ tab    ├───────────────────┐   │  ← the SELECTED tab is elevated, and
  │ └────────┤                   │   │    blends from its right border into
  │ │ tab    │   the note        │   │    the note container: one shape, no
  │ │ tab    │                   │   │    seam
  │ └────────┤ [note toolbar]    │   │
  └──────────┴───────────────────┴───┘

Three pieces, and they are separable:

1. THE NOTES CARD (the main window). Rounded container. Header reads
   "Notes  [flex space]  [↗ button]"; the button opens the Craft app on this
   machine. Under the header, the tabs run VERTICALLY, not horizontally.

2. THE TAB LIST. One row per note. Each carries an X on its right for closing.
   Rename and Delete live in the right-click menu. Double-clicking the selected
   tab's name edits it in place — no alert sheet (today's rename is an .alert,
   which is the wrong weight for renaming a scratch note).

3. THE NOTE CONTAINER. Floats above the notes card, joined to the selected tab.
   Its own toolbar along the bottom — the same copy/export/clear footer the
   widget has today. Selection defaults to a NEW empty note on open, or the
   last note worked on.

The hard part is 1+3's SEAM: the selected tab and the note container are drawn
as separate elevated surfaces but must share a continuous silhouette where they
meet, with no border between them. That is a single-path-shape problem, not two
rounded rects abutted — abutting them shows a hairline and the wrong shadow.
Expect a custom Shape, and expect the elevation (shadow/material) to be drawn
once over the union rather than per-piece.

Scope note: this is CHROME. Nothing here touches markdown-as-truth, the Craft
sync design (ccp-xgl / ccp-2zi.5 / .6), or NoteStore. It can land in parallel
with the sync work and should — it is what the user sees.

Naming: "Scratchpad" becomes "Notes" everywhere CCP owns the name — widget
descriptor, gallery, file names, adapter. Sources/Vorssaint keeps its own
ScratchpadService untouched (never edit upstream). Decide in the rename child
whether the CCPKit adapter stays ScratchpadAdapter (it wraps upstream's
document, whose stored key must not change or every existing note is orphaned)
or renames with a migration.
close_reason: 5/5 children shipped and merged to main: rename without orphaning (ydo.1), vertical card+tab list (ydo.2), joined silhouette with animated join (ydo.3), in-place rename (ydo.4), floating note container with bottom toolbar (ydo.5)

title: standard edit shortcuts do nothing in the panel — no main menu under .accessory
design:
⌘C / ⌘V / ⌘X / ⌘A / ⌘Z do nothing anywhere in the panel, including the markdown
note editor. Reported by the user 2026-09-05.

Cause, near-certain and cheap to confirm: ControlCenterProApp sets
`.setActivationPolicy(.accessory)` (ControlCenterProApp.swift:22) and the app
never installs an NSApp.mainMenu. Those shortcuts are not implemented by
NSTextView — they are key EQUIVALENTS carried by the standard Edit menu items,
dispatched by NSMenu before the responder chain sees them. No menu, no
dispatch, so the keystrokes fall on the floor even though the panel is key
(ControlPanelWindow.canBecomeKey is true) and the text view is first responder.

Fix, framework-first per CLAUDE.md: install a real application main menu with an
Edit submenu whose items carry the standard selectors — undo:, redo:, cut:,
copy:, paste:, pasteAsPlainText:, delete:, selectAll: — plus an App menu
(Services, Hide, Quit) which an .accessory app still benefits from. AppKit then
does the dispatch, and Services, dictation and the emoji picker come along free.
Do NOT hand-roll a performKeyEquivalent override on the panel: it is a switch
statement that has to grow one case per shortcut and gets the disabled/enabled
state wrong.

The menu is never *displayed* under .accessory, so it costs nothing visually.

Verification: the shelf panel and the QuickToggles popovers are also
nonactivating NSPanels — check ⌘C works in each, not just the note editor.
Add a CCPUITests case asserting the Edit menu exists with the expected
selectors, since nothing on screen proves it.
close_reason: installed an application main menu (never drawn under .accessory) with the standard App and Edit submenus. Cause was as diagnosed: no NSApp.mainMenu meant nothing dispatched the standard key equivalents. Verified live — CGEvent-driven cmd+A/cmd+C in the running panel's note editor returned the pad's markdown on the pasteboard. CCPUITests asserts the selectors and the shift-Z split.

title: ask upstream to make MarkdownEngine's block AST and per-range editability public
design: Verified against the 0.12.0 checkout 2026-09-05: BlockNode/ListItem/ExtensionBlockNode are all internal (Parser/ exports two NSAttributedString.Key symbols only), and isEditable is whole-view NSTextView state passed through NativeTextViewWrapper — but the coordinator already implements textView(_:shouldChangeTextIn:) (NativeTextViewCoordinator+TextDelegate.swift:746), so CCP can veto edits into inert ranges from outside; caret-entry and styling still need upstream guidance. Draft issue text below — DO NOT post without the user's go-ahead.
notes:
THIRD ASK ADDED 2026-09-04 (see ccp-prk): tag syntax.

The extension protocol offers InlineSyntax (fixed open/close string literals,
single-line by contract) and BlockSyntax (one fence prefix at column 0 that both
opens and closes). Neither can express an XML-ish tag:

  <callout> … </callout>          multi-line, and open != close
  <comment id="abc"> … </comment> a varying attribute inside a fixed String
  <page><pageTitle>…</pageTitle>  nested

These are Craft's markup, and Craft is not unusual here — any host syncing to a
notes backend with richer blocks than markdown hits the same wall. The ask is a
third syntax form alongside the two: a tag rule with an open name, a close name,
optional attributes handed to contentAttributes, and multi-line content. Framed
as "let an extension describe a tag, not just a delimiter pair."

Lower priority than the other two asks. If it is declined or deferred, nothing
breaks: per ccp-occ those blocks are read-only and subtly marked, which is a
correct and shippable end state rather than a workaround.

Order in the PR: the block-AST visibility ask is the one that unblocks work
(ccp-xgl), per-range inert regions is the one ccp-occ needs, and tag syntax is
the "and here is where this is going" third. Do not let the third sink the first.
DRAFT upstream issue (not posted — needs user's go-ahead): --- Title: Expose the block AST and a per-range editability seam for embedders. Body: Hi — we embed MarkdownEngine as the notes surface in Control Center Pro (macOS menu-bar app, swift-markdown-engine 0.12.0, consumed as a versioned URL dependency). Two things we need that look like general embedder surface rather than our special cases. 1. Public block AST. We sync the document to a backend with addressable blocks, so we need the document structure the editor already computed: BlockNode (with per-block NSRanges), ListItem (range/marker/checkbox/checked/indent/contentRange) and ExtensionBlockNode plus the DocumentAST.parse entry point. Today the whole Parser directory exports two NSAttributedString.Key symbols, so our only option is a second parser — and two parsers means the ranges we sync by and the styling the user sees are computed by different code that can disagree about where a block ends. Ask: public on BlockNode, ListItem, ExtensionBlockNode and the parse entry point. Visibility only, no behaviour change. 2. Per-range inert regions. Some synced blocks are read-only by the backend's rules, and we need regions the caret cannot enter and edits cannot touch. isEditable is whole-view; we can veto edits from outside via textView(_:shouldChangeTextIn:) but caret-entry and styling have no supported seam that we can see. Question first: is this already possible, and if not, would you take a PR adding it? Happy to write the code for both if the shape is agreed. --- End draft.

title: pad history: snapshots before every replacing sync, restorable from a menu
design:
The user's call, 2026-09-04, raised from a narrower worry: MarkdownEngine scopes
undo history by documentId, so a pull that replaces the pad's text underneath the
editor leaves cmd-Z able to walk back into PRE-PULL text — which then gets pushed
as if the user had typed it. Clearing the undo stack on pull fixes the bug and
throws the user's work away to do it. The user asked for the better shape:

  KEEP the pre-pull text, and give the user a way back to it.

## What this is

Every time the pad's text is replaced by something other than typing, snapshot
what was there first. A menu lists those snapshots; picking one restores it.

Snapshot on:
  - a pull that adopts remote text (ccp-2zi.6)
  - a two-way conflict merge, snapshotting the LOCAL side before the merge
  - any future bulk replacement of the pad

Do NOT snapshot on keystrokes. That is what undo is for, and a history full of
every three-second autosave is a history nobody reads.

## Why this is worth more than a bugfix

It subsumes three things that were otherwise separate:

1. The undo-across-pull hazard above. With a snapshot taken, clearing the
   engine's undo stack on pull becomes correct rather than lossy — the pre-pull
   text is not gone, it is one menu item away.
2. ccp-2zi.6's 'Conflicted copy — ' heading, which appends the local version
   INTO the Craft document because 'with no local storage the store is the only
   honest place for a recoverable copy'. That premise dies here. A local
   snapshot is a better place: it does not pollute the user's Craft document
   with machine-generated headings, and it is where the user already is. Revisit
   ccp-2zi.6's conflict design once this lands — this bead does not silently
   change it, but it makes the simpler answer available.
3. It gives the sync an undo at the level the sync operates on. Two-way sync
   without a way back is the thing people are rightly afraid of.

## Shape, to be designed not assumed

Storage: bounded and cheap. A ring of the last N (10?) snapshots per pad, each
{timestamp, reason, full markdown}, alongside the pad's existing persistence.
Pads are short-lived scratch text, so full copies are affordable and diffing
would be premature.

Surface: the scratchpad's footer already carries icon buttons and the tab bar
already carries a per-pad menu. A stock SwiftUI `Menu` of dated entries is the
first thing to try, per CLAUDE.md's reach-for-the-framework rule — not a
hand-built history panel. Each entry needs an accessibility label carrying the
date and the reason, since a bare relative timestamp reads as nothing.

Restoring is itself a replacement, so restoring snapshots the current text
first. That is what makes the menu safe to poke at.

## Open

- Does restoring push? It must not silently overwrite Craft with old text on the
  next debounce without the user knowing that is what restore means. Probably it
  does push, and the answer is that restore is visible and reversible rather
  than that it is inert — but decide it deliberately.
- Whether the snapshot is the whole markdown or the (id, markdown) pairing from
  ccp-xgl. The pairing would let a restore diff back to Craft cleanly instead of
  reading as one big edit; likely the right answer once ccp-xgl exists.

title: markdown to Craft blocks: source-range splitter and the block-id sidecar
description: Cut the pad's markdown into Craft-sized blocks, and keep Craft's block ids stable across syncs. The design field carries the whole approach; ccp-2zi.5 and .6 both depend on it.
design:
The join between CCP's one markdown string and Craft's addressable blocks. Both
push (ccp-2zi.5) and pull (ccp-2zi.6) sit on top of this, so it lands first.

THE FEAR THIS EXISTS TO ANSWER (user, 2026-09-04): pushing the pad as one
markdown body would land in Craft as ONE ENORMOUS BLOCK. A Craft document is
only useful as blocks — handles, drag, collapse, block links — so a sync that
flattens it has destroyed the document even though every character survived.
Nothing in this design may ever write the whole pad as one block.

## Cutting the pad into blocks

swift-markdown (Apple, Apache-2.0, cmark-gfm) parses the pad and every
top-level child carries a SourceRange. Verified 2026-09-04 against the real
parser:

  Heading       lines 1...1    |# Standup|
  Paragraph     lines 2...2    |Ship the **markdown** spike today.|
  UnorderedList lines 4...6    |- [x] resolve the package\n- [ ] see it at 148pt|
  CodeBlock     lines 7...9    |```swift\nlet a = 1\n```|
  BlockQuote    lines 11...12  |> a quote\n> spanning two lines|

So a Craft block's markdown is a VERBATIM SLICE of what the user typed. Nothing
is re-emitted, so nothing is escaped and nothing is lost — the whole class of
round-trip bug the old NoteDocument+Markdown escaping suite defended against
cannot occur, because the text is never regenerated.

One refinement: a list arrives as a single node spanning its items. Craft wants
one block per item, so descend one level into ListItem children, which carry
ranges of their own.

## Keeping Craft's block ids across a sync

A slice has to know which Craft block it IS, or a push degenerates into
delete-and-repost — which changes every block id on every sync and breaks
Craft's block links, backlinks and comments even when the text is right.

The pad therefore carries a sidecar, stored beside it and never shown:

    [(craftBlockID, hashOfTheMarkdownWeLastSawForIt)]

A push diffs the new slices' hashes against that list. Swift's stdlib
CollectionDifference (`difference(from:)`) is the whole algorithm — no
hand-rolled LCS:

    unchanged  →  NO REQUEST AT ALL. Not a PUT, not a no-op write.
    changed    →  PUT /blocks to that id
    inserted   →  POST /blocks with position {siblingId, "after"}
    removed    →  DELETE /blocks by id

Then store the new pairing. Positional matching (Nth slice = Nth block) is NOT
acceptable and must not be the fallback: one insertion in the middle shifts
everything below it and PUTs the wrong text into the wrong ids, which is
corruption rather than churn.

## Why Craft's own blocks survive

The old plan (ccp-2zi.8) preserved blocks CCP has no concept of by MODELLING
them — a sidecar carrying the payload of anything NoteDocument could not hold.
Under markdown-as-truth the mechanism is simpler and stronger:

  PRESERVATION COMES FROM NOT WRITING, NOT FROM MODELLING.

The sidecar's job shrinks from representing a block to merely identifying one.
A slice byte-identical to what we last pulled for that id produces no request,
so whatever Craft holds beyond the markdown — block attributes, styling, its own
metadata — is untouched because nothing wrote over it.

The honest residual, and it needs the user's call before .5 ships: if the user
EDITS a line in CCP whose Craft block carries more than markdown can express,
the PUT flattens that block's extras. Unavoidable in any markdown-truth design,
and bounded to blocks the user actually edited in CCP. Options: accept it, or
mark such blocks read-only in the pad.

## Open, and needing the live connection from ccp-jmk

- Craft blocks with no markdown form at all (an embed, a drawing, a table
  Craft renders specially). What GET /blocks returns for them decides the
  design. They keep their ids in the sidecar to pin position so pushes route
  around them and never delete them, and per the user's decision below they are
  rendered read-only and subtly marked rather than hidden. What Craft actually
  returns for them still needs confirming.
- Nesting. Craft blocks have depth; markdown list indentation maps onto it, but
  a Craft block indented under a non-list parent is a Craft concept with no
  markdown spelling.
- Whether Craft's returned markdown for a text block is byte-stable — if GET
  normalises what we PUT, every block reads as changed forever and the sync
  never quiets. Test this early; it decides whether the hash is over Craft's
  markdown or over ours.

## DECIDED by the user, 2026-09-04: unrenderable blocks are read-only and shown

The residual this bead flagged — editing a line whose Craft block carries more
than markdown can express — is settled. We do NOT accept the flattening, and we
do NOT hide the block.

A block whose content CCP cannot faithfully render as markdown is READ-ONLY in
the pad, and SUBTLY MARKED as such in the UI. The user can see their Craft
content is there and can see that CCP is not the place to edit it. Subtle is the
operative word: a quiet affordance in the pad's own vocabulary, not a warning
banner and not a broken-image placeholder.

This replaces the earlier preference for rendering holes as nothing. A hole the
user cannot see is a hole they will type over the top of and wonder where their
table went. It still pins position so a push routes around it and never deletes
it — the change is that it is now visible and inert rather than invisible.

Consequences to carry through:
- The push side never PUTs a read-only block. It is not "unchanged by
  coincidence", it is unwritable by rule, and the diff must treat it that way
  so a hash collision or a normalisation quirk can never make one writable.
- The editor needs a notion of an inert region. MarkdownEngine's own seams
  (isEditable is whole-view, so this is likely a per-range concern) need
  checking before the UI is designed — that check belongs to the UI bead.
- What counts as unrenderable is decided against a live connection (ccp-jmk),
  not guessed.
notes:
CORRECTED 2026-09-04 by Craft's own API docs — see harness/reference/craft-connect-api.md.
Three things in this bead's design were wrong or unknown and are now settled.

1. "One request per changed block, always" is WRONG. All three write endpoints
   take arrays: PUT /blocks {blocks:[{id,markdown}]}, POST /blocks {blocks:[…]},
   DELETE /blocks {blockIds:[…]}. A push is THREE requests, not N. This matters:
   the space budget is 100 requests/60s and 50/10s per IP, shared with every
   other client in the space, so per-block requests were a real hazard rather
   than merely chatty. The rule that survives is the one that mattered — never
   write the pad as ONE BLOCK — and batching does not weaken it.

2. Nesting is answered. Craft spells depth as 2 leading spaces per level in the
   markdown field, so markdown list indentation maps onto Craft depth directly.

3. The markdown field is NOT plain CommonMark. Craft carries what markdown
   cannot express as inline tags — <page>, <callout>, <caption>, <highlight
   color>, <comment id>, block:// and date:// links, $latex$ — which come back
   on read and are accepted on write. A separate set is OUTPUT-ONLY and cannot
   be written back at all: <collection>, <collectionItem>, <property>, <title>,
   <properties>, <contentPreview>, <itemsPreview>.

   That last set gives ccp-occ a documented rule instead of a judgement call: a
   block whose markdown contains an output-only tag is read-only because the API
   will not accept it back. Same for [text](invalid:out_of_scope), which is what
   an out-of-scope block link returns — PUT it back and the link is destroyed.

   It also raises a question this bead did not have: the round-trippable tags
   will sit in the pad's text as literal <callout> markup, which MarkdownEngine
   renders as plain text. Visible XML in a scratchpad is bad. Options are to
   hide them via an extension (MarkdownEngine has an ExtensionRegistry and a
   fenced-block extension seam), to render them, or to treat tag-bearing blocks
   as read-only too. Decide before the pull side ships.

Still unrun and still the thing that decides where the hash goes: whether GET
returns byte-stable markdown for what we PUT. Needs a throwaway document.
BYTE-STABILITY ANSWERED, 2026-09-04, against a live throwaway document. This was
the open question that decided where the hash goes. Sixteen cases posted, read
back, re-written and deleted; the document was restored to its exact prior state.

CRAFT NORMALISES. Three rewrites observed:
  _italics_                  ->  *italics*
  ==highlighted==            ->  <highlight color="yellow">highlighted</highlight>
  ---                        ->  ***

CRAFT ALSO SPLITS. One input block can become several:
  "- parent\n  - child"      ->  two blocks, the child keeping its 2-space indent
  "first para\n\nsecond para"->  two blocks

Survived byte-identical: plain paragraphs, ## headings, **bold**, `code`,
[links](url), > blockquotes, ```swift fenced code with its language, - bullets,
1. numbered, explicit <highlight color="green">, and trailing whitespace.

AND BOTH TASK-LIST STATES SURVIVE EXACTLY — "- [ ] open" and "- [x] done" come
back unchanged, with listStyle "task". That is ccp-hw0 resolved: the round trip
this project has been failing since Foundation's parser ate the checkbox works
correctly against Craft.

## The decision this forces, and it is a good one

Hash CRAFT'S markdown, never ours. Our own text is not a fixed point — a pad
where the user typed _italics_ would read as changed on every single sync and
the loop would never quiet, which is exactly the failure this bead feared.

Craft's normalised form IS a fixed point: re-PUTting all 18 blocks exactly as
returned changed nothing, and a subsequent GET agreed with the write response
for every block. So the sync quiets after one pass.

No extra GET is needed to learn the canonical form. EVERY WRITE RESPONSE ECHOES
THE NORMALISED MARKDOWN AND THE ASSIGNED IDS. Build the sidecar from the write
RESPONSE, not from what was sent. This is not an optimisation — because a POST
can split one sent block into several, pairing sent-slices to returned-ids
positionally goes wrong from the first split onward. Splitting our own slices
per list item (already the plan) avoids provoking it, but the sidecar must be
built from the response regardless.

Consequence for the diff: after a push, the pad's text and Craft's markdown
differ by the normalisation. Either accept that the next pull rewrites _x_ to *x*
under the user's caret, or write the normalised form back into the pad as part
of the push. The second is more honest and keeps one truth; decide in ccp-2zi.5.

## POST request shape, corrected

position goes in the BODY, not the query string. Query params 400 with
invalid_union:
  {"blocks":[{"type":"text","markdown":"…"}],
   "position":{"position":"end","pageId":"<docID>"}}
Claimed only to record the round-trip findings, not implemented — returned to open 2026-09-04. The design is now COMPLETE: the splitter's source, the hash's side, the sidecar's construction and the batching are all settled and written above. What is left is writing it. Blocked on ccp-jqj only for the parser (the fallback of adding swift-markdown is written up there and unblocks it immediately if upstream declines).
2026-09-05: parser unblocked by the fork (ccp-aa5) — use DocumentAST.parse(_:extensions:) from MarkdownEngine 0.12.0-ccp.1, no swift-markdown fallback needed. Proven reachable by EngineBlockASTTests (gap-free tiling). Still open per the bead: hash side (Craft's markdown), sidecar from write responses, batching.
close_reason: Splitter (verbatim slices, lists descended per item, blanks skipped) plus sidecar (SHA-256 over Craft's markdown, CollectionDifference push plan, read-only pinning by rule) plus per-pad UserDefaults store with rescue copy. 30 tests incl. hw0 splitter-half (both to-do states byte-identical); full hw0 round-trip waits on the pull join (.6), which stays open. Review fixes in: edited blocks anchor inserts, code samples don't classify, isWritable naming, policy split out. Wrapped-line items stay per-line (Craft splits the same way; response rebuilds the pairing). Unblocks .5/.6.

title: adopt swift-markdown-engine and make markdown the pad's truth
design:
DECIDED and PROVEN on branch spike/markdown-engine (commit 72e0355). Whoever
picks this up is finishing an adoption, not evaluating one. The survey behind
the decision is ccp-zaj.

## What is already true on that branch

- Package.swift takes nodes-app/swift-markdown-engine at exact 0.12.0, a URL
  dependency (Apache-2.0, one-way compatible with our GPL-3.0-or-later). Its
  resolution also pins HighlighterSwift and SwiftMath; we link neither, taking
  only the dependency-free MarkdownEngine core product. Documented in CLAUDE.md.
- Sources/CCPUI/DesignSystem/MarkdownNoteEditor.swift is the ONE file that names
  MarkdownEngine — the same rule the CCPKit engine adapters follow. It retunes
  the engine's full-window defaults for a lane-width card: heading ramp
  flattened to [1.35, 1.2, 1.1, ...] from its own [2.0, 1.5, ...], paragraph
  spacing tightened, theme mapped onto CCP's label colours.
- ScratchpadWidget uses it in place of PlainTextEditor. The pad's text was
  already a String, so this was a Binding<String> for a Binding<String> — no
  model change.
- Gate green, 236 tests.

Proven on the running app, not argued: it draws correctly in the 148pt card,
the markers hide themselves until the caret lands on them, and it TAKES THE
KEYBOARD IN THE NON-ACTIVATING PANEL. That last was the risk; it is an
NSTextView, the same reason ScratchpadMarkdownPreview already worked there.

## What is left

1. ccp-xgl — the markdown/Craft block join. Do this first; .5 and .6 sit on it.
2. Delete the block model and the preview path (its own bead).
3. ccp-2zi.5 and .6, rewritten around ccp-xgl.
4. Tuning the spike surfaced: too much air between a paragraph and the list that
   follows it, at this size. Engine list spacing assumes a full window.

## Two things to decide, not to discover

- The format bar. With live markdown the marker IS the command, so
  NoteEditor's bar and block menu have no job. Discoverability and the
  accessibility labels both argue for keeping something — marker insertion
  rather than block commands. Not yet designed.
- Theming is NSColor-based and headings are a fixed fontMultipliers ramp,
  against CLAUDE.md's lean toward semantic Dynamic Type. The spike takes the
  fixed ramp because the card has no room for a 2.0x H1. Resolve deliberately.
notes:
Left in_progress on branch spike/markdown-engine (2 commits, gate green). The spike is done and proven — the editor is wired into ScratchpadWidget and works. What remains is the design field's list: ccp-xgl first, then ccp-s63's deletion, then .5/.6. Nothing is half-applied; the branch is a coherent stopping point and main is untouched.
Tuning item 4 ("too much air between a paragraph and the list that follows it,
at this size") is WITHDRAWN — measured 2026-09-04 and it is not a defect.

Measured on the full-resolution capture, not a scaled crop. Gaps in 2x pixels:
line-to-line 16, paragraph -> list 56, list -> blockquote 47.

Two things the eye got wrong:
- The ~50px gaps are BLANK SOURCE LINES. The pad's markdown has \n\n before the
  list and before the blockquote. In a live-styled editor a blank line the user
  typed is a line the user sees. Rendering it is correct; collapsing it would be
  the bug, and would make the caret's position stop matching the text.
- The two gaps are not "two different amounts doing the same job" (a design
  reviewer's reading at 60 vs 95 off a downscaled crop). They are 9px apart,
  which is the paragraph spacingFactor applied after a paragraph and not after a
  list item. Consistent, not arbitrary.

No change to MarkdownNoteEditor's ParagraphStyle. Leave spacingFactor at 0.15.

MarkdownEngine 0.12.0 pinned, MarkdownNoteEditor is the one file naming it, ScratchpadWidget uses it, the pad is 300pt (ccp-ydj) and the old block model and preview path are deleted (ccp-s63). title: confirm the Craft auth scheme against a live connection
description:
The docs never name an auth header. All they say is 'Create an API connection in the Imagine tab in Craft, and paste your API URL here', which reads as the URL itself being the credential — a per-connection secret path.

Nothing in ccp-2zi.3 can be written until that is confirmed against a real connection: whether there is a header at all, what the URL looks like, and what an unauthorised response is.

TRAP: api.craft.co is a different company (Craft.co, company data) and searches will confidently offer its x-craft-api-key header. It has nothing to do with craft.do.

Needs the user: create a space-scoped connection in Craft and report the URL's shape.
notes:

description:
NoteEditor renders every block kind correctly but nothing in the UI can reach them — only inline marks can be applied, so a user cannot actually make a list.

', '[] ' at the start of a line becomes the block it names. Autoformatting is the one that will get used; the explicit command is what makes it discoverable and what a selection of several blocks needs.

The format bar appears on selection today; a block command has to work with only a caret, so its placement is an open question rather than another button in that bar.

title: plan two-way Craft sync before writing any of it
description:
Investigate and produce a written plan. No sync code starts until this closes — user's explicit call.

What the plan has to settle:

- Craft Connect API reality: auth model and token lifetime, actual endpoints for list/read/write/create/delete, rate limits, whether a whole-document body replace exists or it is delete-plus-POST /blocks, what a document's modified timestamp is and whether it is trustworthy for last-writer-wins. Read the real API docs (connect.craft.do/api-docs); do not design against the search summary in the session that filed this.
- The block mapping, both directions: which Craft block kinds the rich-text model (ccp-2zi.1) maps onto, and what happens to a Craft block CCP has no concept of. A round-trip that silently drops the user's Craft formatting is worse than not syncing.
- Conflict: both sides changed since last sync. Detection, and where the losing text goes so it is recoverable rather than gone.
- Timing: push debounce, pull on activate(), and what happens to a pad being edited when a pull lands.
- Failure and offline: with no local text storage (ccp-2zi.4), what the widget shows when the store cannot be reached, and how typing is prevented from destroying a note that never loaded.
- First-run: existing pads in UserDefaults today. Migrate into Craft, or discard.

Output: design notes on this bead, and whatever ccp-2zi.5/.6 need rewriting into.
design:
Read from the real docs (connect.craft.do/api-docs and its space/ and documents/
sub-pages), 2026-09-04. Everything marked UNCONFIRMED needs a live connection
before code depends on it.

## 1. What the API actually is

Craft Connect is not one API. A *connection*, created by the user in Craft's
Imagine/Connections tab, has a scope, and the scope decides what exists:

  space scope       /documents GET POST DELETE, /documents/move, /folders GET
                    POST DELETE, /tasks, plus all the block endpoints
  daily-notes scope daily notes and tasks
  selected-docs     block endpoints only, inside documents the user picked by
                    hand. NO POST /documents.

DECISION: CCP requires a space-scoped connection. One document per pad means
creating documents, and only space scope can. Under selected-docs the user
would have to hand-make a Craft document per pad and reconnect — not a feature,
a chore.

Endpoints CCP needs:
  GET  /connection            space metadata, urlTemplates, and the server's
                              own UTC clock
  GET  /documents             ids and titles; ?fetchMetadata=true adds
                              createdAt and lastModifiedAt
  POST /documents             {documents:[…], destination: "unsorted" |
                              "templates" | folderId}. Creates them EMPTY —
                              content is a separate POST /blocks.
  GET  /blocks               ?id=&maxDepth=-1&fetchMetadata=true
  POST /blocks               {blocks:[…], position:{pageId,"start"|"end"} or
                              {siblingId,"before"|"after"}}
  PUT  /blocks               partial update; "only the fields provided will be
                              updated"
  DELETE /blocks             by id

THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE EPIC: for text blocks, PUT/POST take **markdown**,
not a bespoke block JSON. NoteDocument already has a markdown bridge from
ccp-2zi.1, round-trip tested. The mapping is written.

SECOND FINDING: the epic's fear — "a naive debounce-append duplicates the note
every 3 seconds" — was aimed at an API with no update. PUT /blocks updates in
place by id, so a push is a diff (PUT changed, POST new, DELETE removed), not a
replace. No delete-then-repost, and no rewriting blocks nobody touched.

Undocumented, and to be treated as hostile: rate limits, request size limits,
error bodies. Any non-2xx is "store unreachable" with backoff, never anything
destructive.

TRAP for whoever picks this up: api.craft.co is a DIFFERENT COMPANY (Craft.co,
company data), and searches surface its `x-craft-api-key` header confidently.
It has nothing to do with craft.do. Do not let a search result point the auth
work there.

## 2. Auth (rewrites ccp-2zi.3)

The docs say only: "Create an API connection in the Imagine tab in Craft, and
paste your API URL here." No header is documented anywhere. So the API URL
appears to BE the credential — a per-connection secret path.

UNCONFIRMED and blocking: the actual scheme. ccp-2zi.3 cannot be written until
the user makes a real connection and we see the URL's shape.

What .3 becomes: not "a token plus a space/folder picker". It is a connection
URL, held in Keychain because the URL is the secret, plus a folder chosen from
GET /folders. Everything else in .3 stands.

## 3. Block mapping, both directions

Push is NoteDocument → markdown → text blocks. Pull is blocks' markdown →
NoteDocument. One conversion, already tested.

Craft has ~14 block types. CCP's model has an equivalent for text, code and
line (divider) and nothing at all for image, video, file, drawing, whiteboard,
table, collection, richUrl or page. A round trip that reads a document into a
NoteDocument and pushes it back would DELETE every one of them.

RULE: CCP never deletes or rewrites a block it did not create.

The store keeps a sidecar per pad — the Craft block ids CCP owns, in order —
and blocks not in it are neither shown in the pad nor touched by a push. The
sidecar is configuration, so UserDefaults holds it without breaking the
no-local-text rule; it is rebuilt from a fresh GET /blocks whenever it stops
lining up.

Why the sidecar and not ids on the model: NoteDocument has no block identity on
purpose — content is the whole value, which is what makes equality mean
"nothing to write". Pairing a block with a backend id is the backend's
bookkeeping. Keeping it in CraftNoteStore is what ccp-2zi.4's "if the protocol
mentions a block, it has leaked" is asking for.

The cost: a pad can be a partial view of its Craft document without saying so.
The widget has to show "3 blocks not shown here" — that lands in ccp-2zi.7.

## 4. Conflict: both sides changed

Detect: per pad, keep lastSyncedAt (the server's lastModifiedAt as of the last
successful sync) and a hash of what was pushed. On activate, GET with
fetchMetadata=true. Remote lastModifiedAt newer than lastSyncedAt AND local
edits not yet pushed = both changed.

Resolve: nothing loses. The local version is appended to the Craft document
under a "Conflicted copy — <date>" heading, then the remote is adopted. With no
local storage there is nowhere else to put a recoverable copy, and the store is
the honest place for it — the user finds it in Craft, where they already are.

Clocks: compare against the server's utc from GET /connection, never the Mac's.
A skewed machine must not win every conflict.

## 5. Timing

Push: 3s debounce from the last keystroke, PLUS a flush on deactivate() and on
app terminate. A debounce that only fires while the panel is open loses the
last three seconds of every session, which is exactly the text the user typed
before closing the panel.

Pull: on activate(). Nothing else — no polling. Idle cost with the panel shut
is a stated feature of this app.

A pull landing on a pad being edited: it doesn't. A pull arriving while the pad
has unpushed edits is the conflict case above, not a silent replace.

## 6. Failure and offline

The widget renders three states, and only one of them is editable:

  loading      the note has been asked for and has not arrived
  ready        editable
  unreachable  offline, unauthenticated, or the store said no

THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE IN THIS PLAN: the editor is disabled until the note has
actually loaded. With no local truth, an empty editor over a failed read is the
one thing that destroys a note — the pad looks blank, the user types, and the
debounce pushes it over the real one. No text, no typing.

Unauthenticated is a normal state with a "Connect Craft" affordance, not an
error. A missing permission never blocks the panel, and neither does this.

## 7. First run

Pads live in UserDefaults today, under keys shared with upstream Vorssaint's
floating pad (the ccp-2zi.1 hazard).

Migrate, once, on the first successful connection: each pad becomes a Craft
document. The UserDefaults text is LEFT IN PLACE, not deleted — upstream's
floating pad keeps working off it, and a migration that went wrong has not
eaten anything.

NEEDS THE USER'S CALL: after migration CCP stops writing those keys, so the
menu-bar pad and upstream's floating pad stop sharing a note. That is a real
behaviour change and it belongs in PATCHES.md either way.

## 8. What .5 and .6 become

ccp-2zi.5 (push): no longer "replace-body". Diff against the sidecar — PUT
changed blocks, POST new ones, DELETE the ones CCP created and the user
removed. Debounce plus deactivate/terminate flush.

ccp-2zi.6 (pull): GET on activate with fetchMetadata, adopt when clean,
conflict-append when not. Owns the sidecar rebuild.

New work this uncovered: confirm the auth scheme against a live connection
(blocks .3), and "N blocks not shown" in the widget (folds into .7).

Two things still need the user: creating that connection, and whether the pad may stop sharing a note with upstream's floating pad after migration.

title: Craft push: debounced block diff, one document per pad
description:
Push the pad to its Craft document ~3s after the last keystroke, and again on deactivate() and app terminate — a debounce that only fires while the panel is open loses the last three seconds of every session.

Not a replace-body. PUT /blocks updates blocks in place by id and takes markdown for text blocks, so a push is a diff: PUT the changed blocks, POST the new ones, DELETE the ones CCP created and the user removed. Blocks CCP did not create are never touched.

The block ids live in CraftNoteStore's sidecar, not on NoteDocument — see the plan on ccp-2zi.8, which this bead is written from. The markdown conversion already exists (NoteDocument+Markdown, ccp-2zi.1).
design:
REWRITTEN 2026-09-04 for markdown-as-truth (ccp-dn5). The block diff this bead
is named for now lives in ccp-xgl — read that first; this bead is the network
half only.

The pad's text is markdown. ccp-xgl turns it into (craftBlockID, markdown)
pairs and tells you which ones changed. This bead spends those:

  changed    PUT    /blocks   to the id
  inserted   POST   /blocks   position {siblingId, "after"}
  removed    DELETE /blocks   by id
  unchanged  nothing. No request at all — that is what preserves the parts of
             a Craft block markdown cannot express.

NEVER write the pad as one block. A single POST of the whole body lands in
Craft as one enormous block and destroys the document's structure even though
every character survives. One request per changed block, always.

Debounce ~3s from the last keystroke, per the epic. A push that fires while
another is in flight coalesces rather than queues — the newest text is the only
text worth sending.

One Craft document per pad. Creating one needs a space-scoped connection
(ccp-2zi.8) and POST /documents, which creates it EMPTY — content is a separate
POST /blocks.

Failure is never destructive: any non-2xx is "store unreachable", back off, and
leave the sidecar untouched so the next push re-diffs from the last state we
actually confirmed. A half-applied diff must not be recorded as applied — write
the sidecar only for the requests that returned 2xx.
notes:
2026-09-04, from the live round trip (see ccp-xgl): Craft rewrites some markdown
on write — _x_ becomes *x*, ==x== becomes a <highlight> tag, --- becomes ***.
So after a push the pad's text and Craft's stored markdown differ.

Decide here, and it is a user-visible choice:
  (a) leave the pad alone, and let the next pull rewrite the user's _italics_ to
      *italics* underneath their caret, or
  (b) write the normalised form back into the pad as part of the push, so there
      is one truth and the surprise happens at the moment they synced rather than
      at some later pull.

(b) is more honest and keeps the sidecar's hash matching what is on screen.
Either way the sidecar hashes CRAFT'S markdown, taken from the write response,
which already echoes both the canonical text and the assigned ids.

Also corrected: POST /blocks takes position in the BODY, not the query string —
{"blocks":[…], "position":{"position":"end","pageId":"<docID>"}}. In the query
string it 400s with invalid_union.

title: beads never export issues.jsonl — the ledger is invisible to git
description: psymail-mini syncs its ledger by committing .beads/issues.jsonl alongside code; its origin has no refs/dolt/data, so git IS the transport. CCP has no issues.jsonl at all: .beads/config.yaml lacks the 'export: auto: true' block (and sync.remote), so bd never writes the export and every bead filed here is invisible to git and lives only in the local embedded Dolt DB. Root cause is upstream in harness-starter — commands/add.sh runs 'bd init' and stops, and bd's default config ships the export block commented out ('Disabled by default'). psymail-mini's config was hand-edited 3 minutes after its bd init (Aug 10 19:10 -> 19:13); that hand edit is the step the harness extraction never captured.

title: README links upstream's docs as CCP's — security reports misroute to Vorssaint
description: The README rewrite (e9cddfb) presents SUPPORT.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CHANGELOG.md as CCP's docs, but all four are still upstream's, untouched by the fork. SECURITY.md sends vulnerability reports to vorssaintapp/vorssaint-utils/security/advisories/new, so a CCP security report lands in the upstream maintainer's private advisories. SUPPORT.md points bug reports at upstream's issue tracker. CONTRIBUTING.md is titled 'Contributing to Vorssaint' and describes upstream's layout, yet README cites it twice as covering CCP's layout and conventions. CHANGELOG.md is entirely Vorssaint releases with no CCP entries.
design: Rewrite SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's (real consequence, and conflicts on upstream merge are rare and cheap). Do NOT overwrite CONTRIBUTING.md or CHANGELOG.md — they are upstream files that keep receiving upstream commits, and overwriting them makes 'merge upstream/main' expensive, which the fork strategy depends on staying cheap. Relabel those two in the README as upstream's instead.
acceptance_criteria: No README link presents an upstream-authored doc as CCP's own. CCP has its own SUPPORT.md and SECURITY.md routing to bubblesunyum/control-center-pro. Docs that stay upstream's are labelled as upstream's.
close_reason: Rewrote SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's own; security advisories now route to bubblesunyum/control-center-pro with an explicit split for vendored upstream sources. README no longer presents CONTRIBUTING.md/CHANGELOG.md as CCP's — labelled as vendored upstream rather than forked, to keep 'merge upstream/main' cheap. Reviewed by reviewer-taste and reviewer-correctness (both clean, all links and claims verified against the repo); scripts/verify.sh passed. Committed 3d28645.

Drop targets: any position in any lane, plus an empty trailing lane that appears as a target to create a new lane.

notes: lr7.2 owns PanelLayout.normalized() (prunes empty lanes, floors at one). Mutation verbs live here, and each must end in a normalized() call — that is what keeps the invariant without lr7.2 shipping the verbs. title: Sticky follow-up: move jitter, grip affordance + hit area, edge-drag, autohide scroller, grip delay
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-09-07 (Vesper): not render cost, not store churn —
coordinate feedback. Both sticky gestures read DragGesture.Value.translation
while the card is transformed by .offset(appliedOffset) / .frame(drawnSize)
from that same translation; SwiftUI converts each event through the dragged
view's current transform, so the card's own motion is subtracted back out of
the next frame. Explains all three symptoms at once: move oscillation, drop
point != finger, and resize appearing ratio-locked (x and y feed back
symmetrically) — which answers the old open Q about "bound to an aspect
ratio": there is no lock, it is the feedback.

Precedent was already in-repo: ControlPanel.resizeTranslation(for:) solved
exactly this for the lane resize by anchoring NSEvent.mouseLocation at press.
Extracted to Sources/CCPUI/Shell/ScreenDragAnchor.swift (engage/translation/
reset/isEngaged, injectable pointer seam); all three drags now use it.

Also: sticky paper border Space.three -> Space.two (16pt), sticky textInsets
-> TextInsets() (per user: "the paper border and get rid of the text's
inset"), gripZone 44 -> Space.three (a 44pt high-priority corner on a 16pt
border reaches 28pt into the paper and eats a caret click on the last line).

SCROLLER SOLVED: it was honest. MarkdownEngine adds caret-comfort bottom slack
sized to the VIEWPORT (percent .5, minPoints 40, ramp from 15%); in a 192pt
sticky it accrues from ~2 lines and by ~7 lines pushes content past the
bottom, so autohide correctly raised a bar on a note whose text visibly fits.
Fixed with MarkdownNoteEditor.stickyOverscroll (percent/max/min all 0) behind
a new defaulted `overscroll` pass-through — Notes passes nothing, unchanged.
With slack zeroed the engine's remaining term is (viewport-content)*ramp,
which can never exceed the viewport, so a bar means real overflow.

TEMP /tmp/sticky-drag.log instrumentation REMOVED from StickyCard,
StickyStore, ControlPanelController (incl. the onChange(of: sticky) tripwire).

Reviews clean: taste no violations; correctness no defects in the rework
(verified commit idempotency across onEnded + GestureState-cancel, the
minimumDistance-0 corner-click guard, anchor reset on every exit, multi-
display continuity, edgeWidth consumers). Acted on both of its process
findings: added a pointer seam + Tests/CCPUITests/ScreenDragAnchorTests.swift
(5 lifecycle tests), and put scripts/ensure-fresh-plan.sh through verify.sh's
`step` so a failed guard says so instead of surfacing as a bare compile error.
Docs updated + blessed. Gate green: 685 tests.

PENDING: user's live feel test. Design review deliberately NOT run yet — it
needs screenshots and the user is testing (bd memory manual-testing-defer-to-
user). Not committed until the user confirms. If move is exact but resize
still feels heavy, the remaining cost is the editor relaying out per frame
(its frame sits outside the StableStickyEditor equatable fence by design);
fallback is to hold the editor at committed size mid-resize and grow only the
paper, committing its frame on release.
close_reason: Root cause was coordinate feedback, not render cost: both sticky gestures read DragGesture.Value.translation while the card was offset/resized by that same translation, so SwiftUI's conversion through the card's current transform subtracted its own motion back out. Fixed by extracting ControlPanel's inline screen-anchor into ScreenDragAnchor and pointing all three drags at it. Also: scroller was honest (MarkdownEngine's viewport-sized overscroll slack — zeroed for stickies behind a defaulted pass-through, Notes unchanged), 16pt paper border with no text inset, corner tick straddling the edge with no hover delay, minimums 136x72, TEMP drag logging removed. User confirmed live: 'it finally works' / 'that's perfect'. Reviews clean; both correctness process findings acted on (pointer seam + ScreenDragAnchorTests, ensure-fresh-plan through verify.sh's step). Commits c72a90b, a9a10b0.

title: pad return should insert a single newline that reads as a new block
design:
User verdict on ccp-inoq (2026-09-05): return producing two newlines is not gonna work, even though the text is correct. Verified in bytes the pad holds single blank-line boundaries (no double-handling) — the complaint is the RENDER: a blank line plus paragraph gap where Craft shows one tight block step. The 

 boundary must go; a lone newline must read as a new block.

LEAD HYPOTHESIS: hard-break syntax. Return inserts two trailing spaces plus newline ("  
") instead of "

". Renders as a single line step with no paragraph gap — the closest markdown gets to Craft's block step. The splitter would learn hard-break as a Craft-block boundary while plain soft-breaks stay same-block (DocumentAST distinguishes them; verify). Fixed-point outlook is good: Craft round-trips trailing spaces byte-identical (reference/craft-connect-api.md), so write echoes resplit identically. RISKS to spike first: trailing-whitespace fragility (user backspaces a space unknowingly and two blocks resume one; other apps strip on paste-in — needs a healing story, likely the existing sidecar churn absorbs it); the engine's marker-hiding may show or strip the spaces (check MarkdownASTStyler); list items already live this way (minted "
- ") and must keep working. REJECTED: U+2028 separator (invisible semantics, taste violation); splitting all single newlines (churns Craft soft-break blocks forever — the ccp-inoq comment on CraftBlockSplitter explains why); negative paragraphSpacing to fake the gap (keeps blank lines in text and copy-out; user already ruled the direction out).
close_reason: Shipped: return mints a hard break ('  \n') instead of a paragraph break, so a single newline reads as a new block with no paragraph gap; splitter cuts hard breaks (soft breaks stay joined, backslash-newline stays soft, marker never ships/fingerprints). Review-fixed: blank-above return steps the caret back onto the new line. Gate 429 green.

title: auto-title a new note from its first content, once, via Apple Intelligence
design:
Specified by the user 2026-09-05. A brand-new note is called "Note 3" and stays
that way, so a vertical tab list of them is a list of numbers. Fix it by naming
the note from what the user actually wrote.

Trigger, exactly once per tab: the note was created empty, content has been
added for the first time, and typing has been idle for 6 seconds. Then summarise
the text into a short tab name and rename the tab. NEVER runs again for that
tab — not on later edits, not on reopen. The once-ness is per-tab durable state,
so it is a field on the pad (an `didAutoTitle` bool, or nil-vs-set on a
`titleSource`), persisted with it — not a runtime flag that resets when the
panel closes.

A user who renames the tab by hand before the timer fires wins: manual naming
cancels the hook permanently for that tab.

## The Apple Intelligence surface

Foundation Models (`import FoundationModels`, macOS 26 — CCP's deployment target
is already 26.0, so no gating needed) gives an on-device
`SystemLanguageModel` + `LanguageModelSession`. On-device matters here: notes
are private, and nothing should leave the machine to get a tab name.

Availability is NOT guaranteed — `SystemLanguageModel.default.availability`
returns unavailable on unsupported hardware, with Apple Intelligence off, or
while the model is downloading. Treat unavailable as the normal state it is: the
note keeps its "Note 3" name, silently. No error UI, no permission card. Check
availability before scheduling the timer, not after it fires.

Ask for a constrained result rather than free prose — a @Generable struct with
one short String field, or guided generation — so the model cannot return a
paragraph that then has to be truncated into nonsense. Cap the name at
ScratchpadDocument.maximumNameLength (40) and run it through
ScratchpadSupport.sanitizedPadName like any other rename.

Inference is async and can be slow; it must not block typing, and if the user
resumes typing while it is in flight, drop the result rather than renaming under
them.

## Fitting the timers

ccp-13f already introduces an idle clock over the note field. This 6s trigger is
a THIRD clock with different semantics again (first-content-then-quiet, once
ever). Build ccp-13f's idle observable so this can subscribe to it rather than
running its own Task — three independent timers over one text field is the smell
CLAUDE.md means by "the moment a flow starts to feel complicated, zoom out".

Depends on ccp-ydo.1 (the rename) only for naming; independent of the chrome.

only lit thing. They come back to full when:
  • the mouse moves over them, or
  • nothing at all has happened — no typing, no scroll, no interaction — for 12
    seconds, or
  • the widgets are hidden (panel closes): reset to normal, never restore into
    a dimmed panel.

Shape it as a CAPABILITY, not a Notes feature — per CLAUDE.md, an override flag
threaded from the note editor into every card is the thing to avoid. The right
seam is a panel-level focus observable that any widget can DECLARE it is being
worked in ("I am the focused work surface"), plus a modifier the shell applies
to everyone else. Notes is the first caller; a future widget with a text field
gets it free.

Two clocks, and they are different — do not collapse them: the ~few-second
delay before dimming is "the user has settled into typing", and the 12-second
one is "the user has stopped doing anything at all". Both are tokens in the
design system, not literals (see ccp-srw).

The fades animate. Nothing about this should snap.

Trap to respect: for-await cancellation does not wake a suspended loop
(bd recall for-await-cancellation-does-not-wake-a-suspended-loop) — the idle
timer must be cancellable at panel close or it fires into a hidden panel, which
is exactly the ccp-2yy bug in another costume.

title: the pad's format bar and heading ramp, both left undecided by the markdown adoption
design:
The two questions ccp-dn5 flagged as "to decide, not to discover" and left open
when the adoption shipped. Neither blocks anything; both are visible in the pad
every day.

## 1. The format bar

With live-styled markdown the MARKER IS THE COMMAND — typing "## " makes a
heading — so the old NoteEditor's format bar and block menu have no job and went
out with ccp-s63. Nothing replaced them.

Two arguments for putting something back, and they are not the same argument:
- DISCOVERABILITY. A user who does not know markdown has no way to learn what
  the pad can do. The pad currently teaches nothing.
- ACCESSIBILITY. "Type ## for a heading" is not an affordance a
  keyboard-and-screen-reader user can discover or a pointer user can click.

If it returns it should insert MARKERS, not apply block commands — the text is
the truth, so a button that types "## " at the line start is honest, and one
that applies a hidden style is a lie about what the document holds.

Worth considering first: whether the footer is the right home at all, or whether
this is a keyboard-shortcut and context-menu concern. MarkdownEngine ships a
ContextMenu; check what it already offers before designing a bar.

## 2. The heading ramp

MarkdownNoteEditor sets a fixed fontMultipliers ramp, flattened to
[1.35, 1.2, 1.1, 1.0, 0.95, 0.9] from the engine's own [2.0, 1.5, …], because a
300pt lane-width card has nowhere to put a 2.0x H1.

This is in tension with CLAUDE.md's accessibility guidance, which leans toward
semantic Dynamic Type so text honours the reader's setting, and reserves the
fixed ramp in STYLE.md for the few places needing a bespoke scale. The card
plausibly IS one of those few places — but that was assumed under time pressure
during the spike, not decided.

The engine's theming is NSColor- and point-size-based throughout, so honouring
Dynamic Type may mean recomputing fontSize from the user's text size and passing
it in, rather than anything the engine does for us. Check whether
NativeTextViewWrapper re-styles when fontSize changes before assuming it is easy.

Note the pad grew to 300pt after the spike (ccp-ydj), so the "no room for a 2.0x
H1" premise is worth re-measuring at the current size rather than inherited.

title: decided: no pluggable parser layer — Craft's markup is markdown plus a tag layer
design:
A decision record, closed on filing. Asked by the user 2026-09-04: could the pad
work in Craft's markup directly — mapped through the editor library — with
markdown added later for broader support? And should there be a parser system
per app, either a pre-built parser like markdown or a custom one like Craft's?

## The reframe that settles most of it

CRAFT'S MARKUP IS NOT A DIFFERENT LANGUAGE. It is CommonMark plus about six
XML-ish tags. Verified by round trip 2026-09-04: headings, bold, inline code,
links, bullets, numbered items, TASK LISTS IN BOTH STATES, blockquotes and
fenced code with its language all survive byte-identical in both directions. The
Craft-specific part is only <highlight>, <callout>, <caption>, <page>, <comment>
and the output-only collection tags.

So the choice is not markdown OR Craft. It is markdown, plus how much of a small
tag layer we support. "Use Craft's markup now and add markdown later for broader
support" inverts it — markdown is already the broad thing, and Craft's markup is
the superset.

## What MarkdownEngine's extension seam can actually take

The seam is real and public: MarkdownEditorConfiguration.extensions is
[any MarkdownExtension], and the engine handles marker hiding, caret reveal,
incremental restyle and rich copy generically for every extension. Well built.

It offers exactly two shapes:
  InlineSyntax — fixed open/close STRING literals, explicitly single-line
                 ("a newline before the close aborts the match")
  BlockSyntax  — one fence prefix at column 0 that both opens and closes (":::")

Measured against Craft's tags:
  ==highlight==                fits — HighlightExtension already ships
  <highlight color="green">    fits awkwardly — 15 fixed colours = 15 static pairs
  block:// and date:// links   already markdown links; a link-handling concern
  $latex$                      the engine has a LaTeX product (opt-in, SwiftMath)
  <callout>, <page>, <content> DOES NOT FIT — multi-line, and open != close
  <comment id="...">           DOES NOT FIT — varying attribute in a fixed String

So the seam buys highlights and stops. Callouts and nested pages need
attribute-bearing multi-line tag syntax the protocol cannot describe. That is an
upstream feature request (folded into ccp-jqj as a third ask), not a mapping we
can write here.

## Why no pluggable parser layer

- It is one implementation pretending to be two. CLAUDE.md's "prefer a flexible
  capability over a special case" is immediately followed by "don't
  overengineer ahead of need"; an abstraction with one real backend and one
  hypothetical one is that, and the shape we would guess today is unlikely to be
  the shape a second app wants.
- The seam already exists and is called `extensions:`. Someone already built the
  pluggable parser system, generically, having solved caret reveal and
  incremental restyle.
- There is no parser to plug in. The pad's editor IS MarkdownEngine; swapping
  its parser means forking or replacing the editor — exactly the position the
  URL dependency was taken to avoid ("a library we consume unchanged and want
  updates from").
- The deepest objection: markdown-as-truth works because a Craft block is a
  VERBATIM SLICE of what the user typed, so nothing is re-emitted and nothing
  can be lost in translation. That property is the reason NoteDocument was
  deleted (ccp-s63). A parser-mapping layer re-introduces precisely that round
  trip.

## The three tiers, and where we are

TIER 1, now: unknown tags are opaque. A block whose markdown carries a tag we do
  not render is read-only. The pad stays pure markdown; Craft's richer blocks are
  visible but inert; nothing is destroyed. No new machinery. Carried on ccp-occ.
TIER 2, when it annoys: register highlights. Craft normalises ==x== into the tag
  form anyway, so the tag is needed to round-trip at all. ~20 lines, and it is
  the one Craft construct people actually use in notes. Its own bead when wanted.
TIER 3, only if it matters: callouts and nested pages, via upstream. ccp-jqj.

Revisit this decision if a SECOND host app appears with a genuinely different
markup — that is when the abstraction can be designed against two real cases
instead of one and a guess.
close_reason: decision record, filed closed. No pluggable parser layer: Craft's markup is CommonMark plus a small tag layer, the engine's extension seam covers highlights and cannot express callouts or nested pages, and a mapping layer would reintroduce the re-emission that markdown-as-truth exists to avoid. Tier 1 (unknown tags opaque) carried on ccp-occ; tier 3 folded into ccp-jqj.

title: identical blocks are indistinguishable to the hash diff
design:
A watch-item on ccp-xgl's diff, not a blocker for it. Filed P2 by the user's
call, 2026-09-04.

ccp-xgl matches a markdown slice to its Craft block id by hashing the slice's
text. Two blocks whose markdown is byte-identical — a repeated `---`, the same
short bullet twice, two blank-ish paragraphs — therefore hash the same and are
indistinguishable to CollectionDifference. On a reorder it may pair slice A with
block B's id and vice versa.

The text still lands correctly: every block ends up with the right markdown, so
this is not corruption. What breaks is identity — Craft block links, backlinks
and comments pointing at those ids now point at the swapped twin. Bounded to
duplicate blocks that were reordered relative to each other.

Not worth pre-solving. Positional tie-breaking among equal hashes is the obvious
fix if it ever bites, and it is a small change to the diff rather than a
redesign. Revisit if the pad turns out to accumulate repeated separators in
practice.

title: read-only Craft blocks in the pad: inert regions, subtly marked
description: Blocks CCP cannot render as markdown are read-only in the pad and subtly marked as such, so a Craft table or embed is visible but not editable here.
design:
A Craft block whose content CCP cannot faithfully render as markdown — a table
Craft draws specially, an embed, a drawing, or a text block carrying attributes
markdown has no spelling for — appears in the pad but cannot be edited there.
The user's call, 2026-09-04, over the alternative of letting an edit silently
flatten the block on the next push.

Two halves, and the second is the design work:

1. INERT. The region cannot take the caret, and the push side never PUTs it —
   not because it happened to hash as unchanged, but because it is unwritable
   by rule (see ccp-xgl). Check MarkdownEngine's seams first: `isEditable` is
   whole-view, so a per-range inert region may need the package's own support
   or an upstream PR. That check is the first task here, because it decides
   whether the rest is a styling job or a package conversation.

2. SUBTLY MARKED. The user should be able to see their Craft content is present
   and see that CCP is not where it gets edited — without the pad turning into
   a wall of warnings. Subtle in the pad's own vocabulary: something like a
   quiet left rule or a muted ground, at the weight the glass cards already
   use. Not a banner, not a lock icon on every block, not a broken-image
   placeholder. It needs an accessibility label saying it is read-only and why,
   since the visual cue is deliberately quiet — an icon-only or colour-only
   signal fails exactly the reader who most needs the explanation.

What counts as unrenderable is decided against a live connection (ccp-jmk), not
guessed, so this is designed after the pull side knows what Craft actually
returns.

   [text](invalid:out_of_scope) form an out-of-scope block link returns. Craft
   refuses these on input, so the block cannot be written back at all.
2. WRITABLE BUT UNRENDERED — <callout>, <caption>, <page>, <pageTitle>,
   <content>, <comment id="…">. Legal to PUT, but MarkdownEngine draws them as
   literal XML, so the user would be editing angle brackets. Read-only until the
   pad can render them, which per ccp-prk needs upstream support the extension
   protocol does not currently have (folded into ccp-jqj).
3. RENDERED — everything else, which after the round trip is known to be most of
   it: headings, bold, italics, inline code, links, bullets, numbered items,
   task lists in both states, blockquotes, fenced code with its language.
   <highlight> joins this band if and when tier 2 of ccp-prk is built.

Implementation note: the test is "contains a tag we do not render", not a
denylist of known-bad tags. A tag Craft adds next year is then read-only by
default rather than silently flattened — fail safe, not fail open.

The subtle marking and the accessibility label this bead already specifies now
have to carry two reasons, not one: "Craft content CCP can't edit" covers both
bands 1 and 2, and the user does not need to be told which.
